bijian_day_branch.defline: The Twin lives inside your Day Gate, the seat of your partner: you love as an equal, and only as an equal.
bijian_day_branch.reading: At home you want two people deciding and neither one in charge, and you lose patience with a partner who leans on you for every choice. Because equality is how you feel respected, you track who conceded the last argument, and you rarely say so. Your friendships run on the same level terms, and you keep the friends a partner also respects. You grow easier about being looked after once someone has proved they stand level with you.

Love.headline: You love best as an equal, or not at all.
Love.recognition: You fall for people with their own opinions and their own plans, and you lose interest in anyone who needs you to lead. Because a matched partner makes you feel safe, you argue as an equal and keep count of who gave way last. You find it harder to be carried by a partner, even for a day, than to win any argument.
Love.lived: The partners who mattered most to you were strong-willed people with lives of their own, and the ones who leaned did not last. A good relationship of yours turned into a contest at least once, over who apologised first, and you kept that score as carefully as they did.
Love.ahead: Love settles from your mid-thirties into a partnership between two people who each run their own lives. Over these years the tally between you grows shorter, and you find you can lean on a partner without feeling smaller.

Social.headline: Your friends are shared, few and loyal.
Social.recognition: Your closest friends are the ones you and a partner both respect, other couples and old friends who treat your home as a unit. Because respect is what keeps you close to anyone, you let wider acquaintances fade without a word. You keep a small circle, and you can say why each person in it is there.
Social.lived: Through your Home Chapter your closest friendships have been between equals, people who did not need you to rescue them. You gave less time to the friends who wanted looking after, and you kept the level ones.
Social.ahead: From your mid-thirties your circle becomes a shared one, friends who know the two of you as a pair. You spend these years with fewer people than before, and you trust each of them more.

bijian_hour_branch.defline: The Twin lives inside your Hour Gate: your later years rest on a few people who treat you as their equal.
bijian_hour_branch.reading: In later life you keep company only where you are met level, with old friends who became family and with children or younger relatives or someone you train who speak to you as equals. Because dignity matters more to you than comfort, you turn down help that comes with pity. You keep learning through the few people who still argue with you. The circle gets smaller as the decades pass, and you lean on the ones who remain more than you admit.

Family.headline: Your family in later life is chosen as much as born.
Family.recognition: You treat the younger people in your family as equals, and you want their argument more than their care. Because being looked down on is the one thing you cannot bear, you hide a hard week from anyone young enough to fuss. Your family stays close in a level way, and you miss some of the softness it rarely offers.
Family.lived: Your family has come to include people you chose since your late forties, old friends with a key and younger people who treat you as their match. You have kept that circle small on purpose, and you have seen less of the relatives who fussed over you.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you grow into equals who stand beside you and argue back. You keep a smaller family around you in these years than most people do, and you are prouder of it than of anything you own.

Growth.headline: You keep growing through the few who match you.
Growth.recognition: You grow in later life through two or three people who push you as hard as you push yourself. Because you learn only from someone you respect, you ignore advice from anyone who talks down to you. Your progress is slower without that small company, and you notice it within weeks.
Growth.lived: A few equals have taught you most since your late forties, a friend or a colleague who would not let you coast. Whenever you worked alone for long your progress stalled, and you went back to them each time.
Growth.ahead: Your growth from your late forties comes through company, long talks and shared work with people who expect a great deal of you. You stay sharper in these years than most people your age, and you owe it to the few who keep you honest.

bijian_hour_stem.defline: The Twin stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: people see you run your later life on your own terms.
bijian_hour_stem.reading: In later life you run your own affairs and turn down help politely, and the people around you notice. Because standing on your own is how you show who you are, children or younger relatives or someone you train learn self-reliance from watching you. You go on learning new skills long after most people stop. You pay for that independence with a distance the young find hard to cross.

Growth.headline: Your growth keeps going when others stop.
Growth.recognition: You take up new skills in later life with the same seriousness you brought to your first job. Because your own standard is the only one you answer to, you keep raising it long after anyone else is watching. You find it hard to learn beside other people, and you lose some of the help that would come from it.
Growth.lived: You have taken up at least one serious new skill since your late forties, and you have kept at it without an audience. Younger people noticed before you mentioned it, and you have been asked how you do it more than once.
Growth.ahead: From your late forties you keep learning in plain view, and younger people copy the habit from you. You become the person they point to when they talk about starting something new, and you are admired for it more than anyone says.

Family.headline: Your family learns independence by watching you.
Family.recognition: In your family you manage alone and see more than you say, and your relatives know it. Because asking for help feels like losing ground, you keep your troubles to yourself until they are over. The younger people in your family admire you, and you are harder for them to reach than you know.
Family.lived: Your family has watched you handle your own affairs since your late forties, the paperwork and the repairs and the bad weeks alike. You turned down offers of help more than once, and one of the younger people learned to stop offering.
Family.ahead: The people after you take their idea of independence from you, and from your late forties they watch how you manage more closely than they say. You teach them most by example, and the few words you add mean more to them than you expect.

bijian_month_branch.defline: The Twin holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years run on your own effort.
bijian_month_branch.reading: Under everything you do at work sits a need to own it, the skill and the result and the name on it. Because depending on anyone feels like losing yourself, you have built your working life on effort nobody else can claim. You learn the same way, slowly and in full, until a skill is yours to the last detail. You finish later than you would beside one trusted colleague, and you accept the delay as the price of owning the result.

Career.headline: You work best when the whole job is yours.
Career.recognition: You take a task from start to finish and want your name on the result. Because your sense of worth comes from your own output, you lose energy fast in any job where freedom exists only on paper. Your output rises with every piece of real freedom you get, and a manager who checks in daily costs you more than a lower salary would.
Career.lived: You have chosen work you could own outright since your late teens, even when a shared role paid better. At least once you left a job because the freedom it promised was only for show, and you have not regretted it.

Growth.headline: Your skills are yours, and nobody can take them.
Growth.recognition: You grow by mastering things fully, until the skill belongs to you and nobody else. Because you trust only what you have built yourself, you keep going alone long after a teacher would have helped. Your progress is fastest the moment someone you respect works beside you, and you put that moment off.
Growth.lived: Long flat stretches have marked your learning since your late teens, and more than one ended only when you finally learned from someone better. You remember each of those people, and you owe them more thanks than you have given.

bijian_month_stem.defline: The Twin stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work you are seen as the one who carries their own weight.
bijian_month_stem.reading: You built your working life on your own effort, and the people around you have always seen it. Because doing it yourself is how you stay sure of your worth, you take whole tasks and sign your name to them, and you stall wherever credit is shared loosely. You keep your equals close at work, and you have quietly let go of everyone who treated you as junior.

Career.headline: You do your best work as nobody's junior.
Career.recognition: You work best when the task is yours from start to finish and your name is on it. Because your own effort is how you measure yourself, you resent shared credit more than hard work, and you slow down the moment a manager hovers. What you want from a job is a clean scoreboard and nobody holding the other end.
Career.lived: Since your late teens you have been the one handed the job nobody else would finish alone. You have changed teams or roles at least once because someone else took the credit for your work.

Social.headline: Your friends are your equals, or they drift.
Social.recognition: You choose friends who match you, people who carry their own weight and expect you to carry yours. Because you measure everyone against your own standard, you drift from anyone who leans on you, and you rarely say why. You keep a small circle, and you keep it for years.
Social.lived: Your friendships since your late teens have been between equals, often with one friend who mirrors you like a sibling. More than once you have lent money or time to a friend and found it harder to talk about than the friendship could bear.

bijian_year_branch.defline: The Twin lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your early years you learned to rely on yourself.
bijian_year_branch.reading: Your first home expected you to manage, and you were trusted with your own problems before most children are. Because you were trusted young, you came to trust yourself before anyone else, and you worked out much of what you know without asking. The habit makes it hard for you to let people in, at home or anywhere, and you accept help only after you have tried it alone.

Family.headline: You grew up level with the people around you.
Family.recognition: You treat your family as equals, present and practical and never fussy. Because closeness when you were small came from standing side by side, you show tenderness late and mostly through what you do. You turn up to fix a family problem before anyone asks, and you rarely say what you feel while you do it.
Family.lived: In your first home a sibling or a cousin stood beside you as an equal, and the two of you looked after each other. You learned to settle things between yourselves, and the adults were the last to hear about them.

Growth.headline: You grow from trusting yourself first.
Growth.recognition: Every skill you have began with deciding that you could do it. Because you learned early to depend on yourself, nobody can push you into learning, and you take to a teacher only once you have chosen them. You pick things up faster with one other person learning beside you, and you let few people that close.
Growth.lived: You taught yourself things as a child that the adults around you had not shown you, and you kept quiet about how hard it was. By the time you were grown you had a stubborn way of learning, on your own terms and at your own pace.

bijian_year_stem.defline: The Twin stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: your family raised you to stand on your own.
bijian_year_stem.reading: As a child you were noticed for being capable, and help at home was something you earned. Because managing alone won you approval early, people still meet that capable face first, and friends trust you to carry your share. Asking your family or anyone else for something has stayed the hardest thing you do, and you go without more often than the people around you guess.

Social.headline: Your friends are equals, or they are not friends.
Social.recognition: You keep a few equals close and everyone else at a friendly distance. Because you seem to need nothing, you attract people as capable as you are, and the ones who want support look elsewhere. Your circle is small and sturdy, and you feel its gaps more than you admit.
Social.lived: The friends you made as a child were your equals, children who competed with you and stood up for you in turn. The friendships that lasted into your teens were the level ones, and you let the rest go without a fuss.

Family.headline: You are the relative who never needs rescuing.
Family.recognition: You do your part in the family before anyone thinks to ask, and you expect nothing back. Because your first home rewarded self-reliance, you call your relatives when there is something to offer, never when there is something to ask. Your relatives hear from you less than they want, and you mean the quiet as a kindness.
Family.lived: An older relative in your first home made a point of standing on their own, and you copied it before you understood it. You asked for less with each year you grew, and the adults around you praised you for it.

jiecai_day_branch.defline: The Rival lives inside your Day Gate, the seat of your partner: your love life carries real stakes, in money and in pride.
jiecai_day_branch.reading: You are drawn to bold partners with strong opinions and their own way with money, and a mild love has rarely held you long. Because you feel most alive when someone pushes back, your home is lively and loud, full of debate and shared bets. Money is where the two of you clash most, since you both want your way. You keep the peace best where each of you holds an account of your own, and the arguments turn back to love.

Love.headline: You fall for people who push back.
Love.recognition: Partners with a temper, an opinion and plans of their own are the ones you fall for. Because being challenged is how you know you matter to someone, a calm and agreeable partner bores you within months. You keep loving through the arguments, and you count a quiet week as a sign that something has gone wrong.
Love.lived: The people you have loved were strong-willed and hard to predict, and they made you earn every point you won. At least one relationship of yours stayed loud for years, with fights over plans and whose turn it was, and you stayed because it held your interest.
Love.ahead: From your mid-thirties you share a home with a partner as bold as you are, and the house is rarely quiet. Love in these years holds through open argument, and you find more warmth in it than in any calmer bond before.

Wealth.headline: Your money at home is shared, and contested.
Wealth.recognition: You treat money in a relationship as joint, and you give freely when your partner wants something. Because loyalty to the person beside you outweighs any careful plan, the shared accounts blur and the arguments arrive later. You stay calmest about money when your share and theirs are kept apart, and you seldom manage it.
Wealth.lived: Your money has risen and fallen with the people you lived with, generous seasons followed by tight ones. You have paid for a partner's plans more than once, and you found it easier to give than to talk about it afterwards.
Wealth.ahead: Money and love move together in your household from your mid-thirties, and the stakes on both rise. You earn well with a partner in these years, and the arguments ease whenever your money and theirs sit in separate names.

jiecai_hour_branch.defline: The Rival lives inside your Hour Gate: what you build in later life you will share, and sometimes have to defend.
jiecai_hour_branch.reading: Your later life stays loud and full, with children or younger relatives or someone you train arguing with you and for you. Because you value being matched more than being obeyed, you are drawn to the bold ones, and you give them more than you promised yourself. You share most of what you build late, and you hold on to your part only where you fixed its size early.

Family.headline: Your family grows louder, and dearer, with age.
Family.recognition: You are pulled toward the strong-willed people in your family, the ones who push back and want their share. Because you respect whoever stands up to you, you give most to whoever argues hardest, and the quieter ones get less of you. You love a full and noisy table more than a calm one.
Family.lived: Since your late forties your family has grown louder, with younger people who want your time, your backing and your money. You have given more than you meant to, and you would do most of it again.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you will push against you and fight for you. You will find those years warmer and riskier than most people's, and you will be happiest in them when you have kept your own keys.

Wealth.headline: Your later money will always have company.
Wealth.recognition: You treat money as something shared, and you find it hard to say no when someone close asks for help. Because loyalty matters more to you than a full account, you give first and count later, and the counting rarely feels good. You keep wealth best when the limit is fixed before anyone asks.
Wealth.lived: More people have had a claim on your money since your late forties, among them younger people and someone you backed. You have given more than you planned each time, and you have learned which requests to price in advance.
Wealth.ahead: Younger people start to make claims on your money from your late forties. You will give more than you planned each time, and you will keep your own floor only where you set the number before anyone asks.

jiecai_hour_stem.defline: The Rival stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: in later life people see your nerve and ask you to back them.
jiecai_hour_stem.reading: Your later years stay bold and public, and you keep taking risks long after people your age have stopped. Because being in the contest keeps you feeling alive, you say yes to children or younger relatives or someone you train more than you planned, and their ventures keep you learning. You find real joy in some of that backing, and you lose part of what you give because you said yes before you asked what it was for.

Wealth.headline: Your later money goes to the bold.
Wealth.recognition: You back people you believe in, a younger person's venture or a friend's new start, and you give with an open hand. Because daring is what you admire most, a confident request is hard for you to refuse. Your savings shrink in the years you give without counting, and you know which of your gifts were really losses.
Wealth.lived: People with plans that needed money have turned to you since your late forties, younger people and friends alike. You have agreed more often than you meant to, and you have watched some of it pay off and some of it disappear.
Wealth.ahead: From your late forties the people after you start bringing you their plans and asking for support. You spend more on other people's ventures in these years than on your own comfort, and you are glad of most of it.

Growth.headline: You keep growing through the daring young.
Growth.recognition: You grow in later life by watching bold people take risks and judging their bets with an experienced eye. Because risk still interests you, mentoring someone daring keeps your own nerve sharp. You lose interest in cautious company, and you come alive around anyone young enough to try something foolish.
Growth.lived: Your learning since your late forties has come through other people's plans, the ones you advised on and the risks you watched up close. You have grown sharper each time a younger person asked for your judgement, and you have enjoyed being asked.
Growth.ahead: You grow from your late forties by staying involved, advising and backing people who are still at the start. Their risks keep your mind quick in these years, and you take more chances with your own plans than you did a decade earlier.

jiecai_month_branch.defline: The Rival holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years are built on risk and on people who share it.
jiecai_month_branch.reading: Underneath what you do for a living is a need to have something at stake, and waiting has always felt riskier than acting. Because you measure yourself against the people beside you, you do your best work where results are counted in public and shared with partners. Your colleagues and your friends end up as one circle, and your income arrives in surges that you spend on them as fast as it comes. You build more than you keep, and it rarely troubles you.

Career.headline: You work best with something real at stake.
Career.recognition: You are at your sharpest in jobs with clear stakes, sales or ventures or anything where the score is public. Because you need to feel the risk to feel awake, you move first and sort out the rest afterwards. Your bold moves pay best beside a colleague who checks the details, and you have little patience for the checking yourself.
Career.lived: Since your late teens you have chosen work that paid by results over work that paid by the hour. You have had big wins and sharp drops in those years, and you have rarely wished for a duller job.

Wealth.headline: Your money comes in bursts, and leaves with friends.
Wealth.recognition: Money reaches you suddenly and leaves with the people you celebrate with, a friend's venture or a round for the table. Because generosity is how you show you belong, you lend before you are asked and count only later. You save less than you mean to in the good years as well as the lean ones, and you feel it most after a win.
Wealth.lived: Your income has arrived unevenly from your late teens, a good year followed by a thin one. More than once you lent or spent a windfall on friends within weeks, and you have mostly not regretted it.

Social.headline: Work and friendship are one circle for you.
Social.recognition: Your friends and colleagues are mostly the same people, and you go into business with the ones you like. Because you trust the people you enjoy, you agree to shared plans before the terms are clear. When one of those plans fails, you lose the friend along with the money.
Social.lived: Your closest friends since your late teens have also been the people you worked or did deals with. At least one friendship of yours ended over a shared venture, and you still count the friend as a loss more than the money.

jiecai_month_stem.defline: The Rival stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work people see your nerve before anything else.
jiecai_month_stem.reading: You volunteer whenever there is a contest to enter, and the colleague who ranks first is the one you watch. Because winning in the open is how you prove your worth, you climb quickest where results are ranked and stall where credit is pooled. You make friends and allies through the same contests, and you lose some of them as quickly as you made them. Your worst setbacks have come through bets you shared with someone else.

Career.headline: You rise fastest where the score is public.
Career.recognition: You come alive in work that ranks people openly, commissions and targets and anything with a clear winner. Because you need proof that you are winning, a vague team goal leaves you flat and restless. You unsettle quieter colleagues without meaning to, and you do your best work where nobody minds.
Career.lived: Your best jobs since your late teens have been the ones with a clear score, sales figures or rankings or a promotion race. You have left at least one shared project because the prize was never clearly divided, and you have done better alone since.

Social.headline: Your circle is full of rivals you respect.
Social.recognition: Most of your friends come from work, and many of them started as people you competed against. Because you respect anyone who can beat you, your closest bond at work is with a former rival. You lose friends over contests more easily than most people, and you keep the ones who competed fairly.
Social.lived: From your late teens you have made friends through competition, in teams and courses and workplaces where everyone was ranked. More than once a friendship ended when you won, and you have kept the rival who took a loss well.

jiecai_year_branch.defline: The Rival lives inside your Year Gate: in your first home almost everything was shared, and almost everything was claimed.
jiecai_year_branch.reading: As a child you shared a bed or a bike or a birthday with a brother, sister or cousin who wanted their turn. Because nothing at home stayed yours for long, you learned to give quickly and to keep a quiet count. Your family reaches for your help and your money first, and you say yes before you have worked out what it costs.

Family.headline: You grew up sharing everything with family.
Family.recognition: You treat family as people with a natural claim on your time, your space and your money. Because sharing was how your first home held together, refusing a relative feels like disloyalty to you. You give without fuss, and you resent it quietly when the giving is taken for granted.
Family.lived: The money and the clothes and the space were all shared in your first home, and a sibling or cousin was never far from what was yours. Growing up you gave without being asked, and you could tell exactly who had taken what.

Wealth.headline: You give money easily and keep track of it.
Wealth.recognition: You lend to family before you have finished saving for yourself, and you rarely ask for it back. Because money at home was always pooled, a private account feels slightly selfish to you. Your savings grow slowly while your family's claims stay open, and you feel both generous and short.
Wealth.lived: You saw money borrowed and lent around the family as a child, and nothing was ever written down. Before you were grown you had given away more than you could spare, and you had learned which relatives paid you back.

jiecai_year_stem.defline: The Rival stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: you grew up in a bold family where money moved fast.
jiecai_year_stem.reading: People who knew your first home remember its nerve and its charm, the way it won over a crowded table. Because boldness was praised at home, people warm to you quickly, and you act while others are still deciding. You learned to spend as fast as you earn, much of it on friends, and you feel uneasy holding on to money for long.

Wealth.headline: Money moved fast around you from the start.
Wealth.recognition: You spend quickly and generously, and money that comes in through friends or luck goes out the same way. Because a free hand with money was admired at home when you were young, saving feels cautious to you in a way you dislike. Your bank balance swings more than most people's, and you are calm about it until a lean month arrives.
Wealth.lived: Money arrived and vanished in your family while you were growing up, a good year followed by a hard one. You had your own share of that nerve before you were grown, and you spent what you had almost as soon as you had it.

Social.headline: People take to you quickly, and in numbers.
Social.recognition: You make friends fast, and a new group accepts you within an evening. Because charm was your family's way with people, you collect many allies and only a few who would stay through trouble. You know the difference between the two, and you feel it most in a hard year when the crowd thins.
Social.lived: As a child you were popular with other children and with adults, and you were invited to more than your share. By the time you were grown you had a wide circle and one or two close friends who mattered far more, and you knew which were which.
